paper_title: Measurement of light-by-light scattering and search for axion-like particles with 2.2 nb$^{-1}$ of Pb+Pb data with the ATLAS detector
coupling_convention: 1/Lambda_a converted from TeV^-1 to GeV^-1 (equivalent to g_agamma in GeV^-1 in the ALP-photon convention used by the paper)
notes: ATLAS Run 2 Pb+Pb (2.2 nb^-1) light-by-light scattering measurement with ALP search via gamma gamma -> a -> gamma gamma. The paper sets 95% CL upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling 1/Lambda_a ranging from 0.3 TeV^-1 (at m_a ~ 6 GeV) to 0.06 TeV^-1 (at m_a ~ 100 GeV), the most stringent limits to date in the 6-100 GeV mass range. Only the endpoint values quoted in the text were extractable; the full observed limit curve (Figure 9, right) with fine structure (e.g., discontinuity at 70 GeV from bin-width change) is available in HepData but not in the text. Assumes 100% ALP branching fraction into photons. Not a dark matter search, so no local DM density assumption. Cross-section limits (2-70 nb) were also set but the coupling limit is the relevant exclusion.
